# A stage can declare the lock its caller must already hold. The incident: twice in
# one day, four hours apart, by two agents who had each read the other's write-up —
#
#   breeze acquire lock guards-sweep    # refused, someone else has it
#   breeze start stage p verify-guards  # ran anyway
#
# The shell does not couple those two lines, so the serialization only held while
# whoever typed it remembered, at exactly the moment they were busy. breeze owns both
# the lock table and the stage start, so it couples them instead.
env BREEZE_DIR=$WORK/state

exec breeze register identity admin
cp stdout admin.token
exec breeze register identity peri
cp stdout peri.token
exec breeze register identity trail
cp stdout trail.token
exec breeze apply -f pipeline.hcl --as admin --token-file admin.token

# The requirement is legible BEFORE you trip over it. `stage status` deliberately
# cannot answer it (no actor in a status query, so "do you hold it" has no answer),
# which is exactly why it has to be visible here.
exec breeze show pipeline guarded
stdout 'requires lock: guards-sweep'

# Holding nothing: refused, and told to acquire rather than to wait, because nobody
# else has it either.
! exec breeze start stage guarded sweep abc123 --as peri --token-file peri.token
stderr 'requires the resource lock "guards-sweep"'
stderr 'nobody else does'

# Holding it: runs.
exec breeze acquire lock --resource guards-sweep --as peri
exec breeze start stage guarded sweep abc123 --as peri --token-file peri.token
stdout 'succeeded'

# A second actor is refused while peri holds it, and is told WHO has it — "wait for
# them" and "you forgot to acquire" are different situations needing different next
# moves, so the refusal distinguishes them.
! exec breeze start stage guarded sweep def456 --as trail --token-file trail.token
stderr 'held by "peri"'

# Released: the next caller must still acquire it. The gate is about holding the
# lock, not about being the last person who did.
exec breeze release locks --as peri
! exec breeze start stage guarded sweep def456 --as trail --token-file trail.token
stderr 'requires the resource lock "guards-sweep"'
exec breeze acquire lock --resource guards-sweep --as trail
exec breeze start stage guarded sweep def456 --as trail --token-file trail.token
stdout 'succeeded'

# A stage that does not declare one is completely unaffected — this gate is inert
# for every pipeline written before it existed.
exec breeze start stage guarded plain abc123 --as trail --token-file trail.token
stdout 'succeeded'

# A lock requirement on an approval stage would never be enforced, so the config
# would claim a protection that does not exist. Refused where someone is looking at
# the file and can fix it.
! exec breeze apply -f bad.hcl --as admin --token-file admin.token
stderr 'requires_lock is not meaningful on an approval stage'

exec breeze stop

-- pipeline.hcl --
pipeline "guarded" {
  stage "sweep" {
    type          = "command"
    requires_lock = "guards-sweep"
    timeout       = "10s"
    command       = ["/bin/true"]
  }
  stage "plain" {
    type    = "command"
    needs   = []
    timeout = "10s"
    command = ["/bin/true"]
  }
}

-- bad.hcl --
pipeline "wrong" {
  stage "review" {
    type               = "approval"
    required_approvals = 1
    approver_role      = "reviewer"
    requires_lock      = "guards-sweep"
  }
}
